packages/rekordbox-library/src/beat.test.content: The monotonicity test claims to cover "inside and outside the grid", but the generated grid has 128 beats (indices 0..127 → musical beats 1..128) while the loop only reaches beat 80 (`i <= 160` → `i/2`). The upper out-of-grid extrapolation region (beat > 128) is therefore never exercised, so a monotonicity regression in the "after the last anchor" nearest-tempo branch would go undetected. Extend the range past the top of the grid (beat 128 requires `i > 256`).

The out-of-grid samples only reach -0.25..1.25 of the grid span, and the out-of-grid error of a nearest-segment extrapolation grows linearly with distance from the ends. An extrapolation bug that is small within ±25% of the span (e.g. using the wrong end segment's tempo) can stay under the 1e-6 s tolerance here and survive the round-trip property. Consider widening the offset range (e.g. -2..3) so the extrapolation branches are meaningfully stressed.

`expect(Number.isFinite(accumulator)).toBe(true)` only rejects NaN/Infinity; any finite-but-wrong mapping (e.g. a constant value, or an off-by-one beat shift) still satisfies it. Combined with the fact that the timing budget is the only other assertion, this benchmark can pass while the mapping itself is broken. Add a correctness assertion on a known point, e.g. `expect(beatToSourceSeconds(grid, 1 as Beat)).toBeCloseTo(grid.beats[0]!.sourceTimeMs / 1000, 9)` (or accumulate and compare against a reference result).

The 250 ms wall-clock budget is calibrated to a specific host (comment claims 86 ms) and measures cold-JIT code on a shared CI runner. On slower/contended machines this assertion fails for environmental reasons unrelated to any regression, making the suite flaky. Prefer a much looser bound (or warm up before timing) so the test only catches order-of-magnitude regressions rather than host speed.

Exact float equality on a `seconds * 1000` product is brittle and inconsistent with the neighbouring `toBeCloseTo(1473, 9)` assertion for the same conversion. It happens to be exact today, but it will break if the conversion/rounding strategy changes even slightly. Use the same tolerant comparison as the second case.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/agent-api.te.content: The `requests` buffer (and the `requests` field on `FakeAgent`) is populated on every request but never read by any test, so it is dead code. It is also the only place that could verify wire-level token handling (that the `Authorization: Bearer` header is actually sent, that the token never leaks into a query string, and which endpoint path was hit). Either assert on it (e.g. `expect(agent.requests).toContain("/api/data/1234")` and that no request URL contains `TOKEN`) or remove it — as written the recorder gives a false impression that the wire traffic is verified.

Hard-coding `port: 1` to mean "nothing listens" is environment-dependent and flaky: port 1 can be occupied by a privileged service, and a slow/blocked connect is indistinguishable from `ECONNREFUSED` here because `RekordboxAgentClient.get` maps both a socket error and a timeout to `null` -> `{ present: false }`. The test therefore cannot tell a genuine "not-present" from a timeout being misreported (and it also depends on the 300ms budget never elapsing on a loaded CI box). Obtain a guaranteed-free ephemeral port by binding a throwaway server, reading its port, then closing it, and assert the `reason` as well as `present`.
packages/rekordbox-live/src/agent-api.te.existing_code: const client = new RekordboxAgentClient({ port: 1, timeoutMs: 300 });

packages/rekordbox-live/src/agent-api.te.content: The endpoint-failover list is never actually exercised: the fake only answers `/api/data/1234` (== `AGENT_RESOLVE_ENDPOINTS[0]`), and the assertion is pinned to index 0. The resolve loop's fallback behavior (first candidate 404s, a later candidate resolves) is untested, so a regression that breaks the ordering/fallback in `AGENT_RESOLVE_ENDPOINTS` would still pass. Add a case where the fake 404s the first candidate and serves the second, then assert `resolved.endpoint` equals `AGENT_RESOLVE_ENDPOINTS[1]`.

No test ever forces the timeout/abort path: every client is built with a 300-500ms timeout and every fake answers immediately, so `req.on("timeout")` -> `req.destroy()` -> `null` -> `not-present`/`denied` interactions are unverified, and a hung request (e.g. the timeout option being ignored) would surface as a test hang rather than a failure. Add a fake route that delays beyond the timeout and assert the resulting reason is `not-present` (timeout) rather than `not-found`.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/agent-api.te.content: `closeAgent` resolves only when `server.close()`'s callback fires, which waits for all connections to end. `RekordboxAgentClient` issues requests via `node:http`'s default global agent, which keeps sockets alive after each response; the teardown therefore relies on the runtime destroying idle keep-alive sockets inside `server.close()` (Node >= 19). On a runtime that does not, this callback never runs and the suite hangs with a leaked listener. Make teardown explicit, e.g. call `agent.server.closeIdleConnections()` (or `closeAllConnections()`) before/instead of relying on `close()` alone.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/follow.ts.content: Hardcoded business values: the version remedy embeds the literal version `7.2.19` and the date `2026-10-12` directly in the user-facing detail. These drift independently of `supportedVersions` (macOS `["7.2.8","7.2.17","7.2.18"]`, Windows `["7.2.10"]`) and of the upstream coverage, so the assistant can emit stale/misleading remediation guidance (the date is already in the past). Derive the message from a maintained constant/source of truth (or drop the version-specific date) instead of inlining literals.

Destination extraction is unscoped and last-write-wins: the regex matches any IPv4:port substring on any line containing "osc", and `destination` keeps whatever the last such line held. A config with more than one OSC-related address (e.g. an input/listen port such as `osc_input = 127.0.0.1:4461` after `osc_dest = 127.0.0.1:4460`) silently reports the wrong destination, which then produces a false `wrong-destination` setup state (or masks a genuinely wrong one). Scope the match to the destination key so only the intended line can set `destination`.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/follow.ts.content: `subdiv` is only recognized when the entire remainder is exactly the case-sensitive string `beat/subdiv/<n>`. Any casing variation or trailing/extra segment yields `subdiv: null`, and the caller in rkbx-osc.ts then falls through to the path `switch` where the address is dropped into `unknownAddresses` — subdivision-based follow silently stops working with no error surfaced. Consider matching case-insensitively and/or tolerating surrounding segments (or reporting an explicit parse failure) so a malformed subdiv address is observable.

The state mapping only covers the five currently-known step ids and its final fallback silently maps any other failed step to `"no-packets"`. Because `failed` is the first step that fails, adding/reordering a step (or any id mismatch) will produce a wrong state and a remedy that quotes a different step's detail. Prefer mapping via an explicit `Record<RkbxSetupStep id, state>` or deriving the state from the step itself instead of a hand-maintained ternary chain with a catch-all.

Prolink takes precedence over AX based only on `peerPresent` and a non-null `beat`, ignoring `prolink.playing`. A paused/stale remote beat therefore overrides live AX playback (and reports its own `playing:false` to consumers). Per the file's stated intent ("prolink beats win when a peer emits; AX elapsed wins when readable"), please confirm this is desired; if the remote is paused, the AX reading is the honest live source and should win. At minimum exclude `prolink.playing === false` from the prolink branch.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/lighting-ipc.content: This assertion is too weak to prove the decode-failure path. `Buffer.from(str, "base64")` is lenient and never throws, so `decodeLightingCaptureBase64("!!!not-base64!!!")` does not hit the `catch` branch (`capture is not base64`) at all — it silently strips the invalid characters to `notbase64`, decodes 6 garbage bytes, and `decodeLightingCapture` then fails on a bogus huge frame length. `frames` ends up empty, so this test passes even though the intended error-reporting path is never exercised. Also assert `malformed` is non-empty so the rejection is actually verified.

The contract suite is run against a provider created with `fixtures: []`, which the sibling test establishes yields `capability() === "MISSING"` and `onStart()` → `unavailable`. The suite never checks the start/lifecycle path: it reaches `"live"` solely because `ingestEvent()` unconditionally calls `setStatus({ state: "live" })`, bypassing `onStart`. As written, a provider whose start logic is completely broken (e.g. never reports `unavailable`, or fails to transition correctly) would still pass. Exercise the suite with a READY provider (non-empty `fixtures`) and/or add explicit assertions that the MISSING provider reports `unavailable` with the owner `reason`/`remedy` after `start()`.

`"live"` is only asserted after `replayAll()`. A provider that transitions to live solely as a side effect of replay (and leaves `start()` stuck at `"starting"`), or one that never exposes a terminated state on `stop()`, would still pass. Assert the status immediately after `start()` (e.g. `"starting"`/`"unavailable"` expectations) and after `stop()` so the state machine is actually pinned down.

`fixture()` hardcodes `condition: "one-deck"` regardless of the `action` argument, so the `"loop-roll"`/master/loop/hotcue test produces an action/condition pair (`loop-roll-one-deck`) that does not correspond to any real matrix cell. Any downstream validation or path derivation that depends on the action↔condition pairing is therefore silently accepted rather than exercised. Let `fixture()` accept a `condition` parameter and pass a matching value from the call sites.

With only two frames this only checks the first inter-frame gap; dropped/reordered/duplicated intermediate frames, or incorrect cumulative `index * stepMs / rate` accumulation beyond the first step, would go undetected. Add a third event and assert all successive deltas (or the total span) so cumulative timing is validated, not just the first gap.

packages/rekordbox-live/src/memory-reade.content: The lint assertion is too weak to be meaningful. `not.toEqual([])` only proves *some* failure string is produced; it does not verify that missing mandatory fields (`rekordboxVersion`, `platform`, `paths`, `verification`, …) are actually detected, nor which error/issue codes are reported. A regression where `lintOffsetsFile` returns a single generic error for every malformed input (or the wrong fields) would still pass. Assert on the specific linted keys/fields for at least one partially-populated object instead of only checking non-emptiness.

This scanner test is effectively tautological: it writes exactly the values the scanner is meant to discover and then asserts only the *field names* that were found. It never checks the discovered `base`/`offsets`, so a scanner that produced correct field labels at the wrong locations would pass. It also provides only a single observation, so the multi-observation verification branch in `scanMemoryOffsets` (the `rest`/filter path) is never exercised, and there is no negative case (e.g. a candidate value that must NOT be returned). Assert the concrete `{base, offsets}` tuples and add a second observation plus a non-matching value to guard against false positives.

The consent/version gates are only asserted at the `capability()` level. The disabled, no-consent and wrong-version providers are never started and never `poll()`ed, so a provider that still emits decks from the accessor despite a failing gate would not be caught here (only the no-consent case calls `start()`, and only its status is inspected). Start each gated provider and assert that `poll()` / `getDecks()` produce no data; also exercise `start()` on the READY provider to confirm it actually transitions to live.

The harness writes a constant playhead (0.5s) and BPM (128) on every `loadTrack`, and the generated `trackId` is computed but never asserted. As a result, regressions in playhead/time progression (e.g. a frozen or wrongly-reset playhead) and in track-id mapping will pass the suite undetected. Make the playhead/track id vary per generation (e.g. advance the virtual clock and assert `decks[0].playheadSeconds`/`track.id` follow), and add a `cleanup` that actually tears down state if the suite is expected to invoke it.

The slot layout (base `deck`/`region`, indices 0..3 mapped to playhead/bpm/masterDeck/trackId) is hardcoded independently here and again in the contract-suite `loadTrack`. If the offsets layout changes, one of the two sites can silently drift and the tests would no longer reflect the real schema. Extract a shared helper (or derive indices from the `offsets()` fixture) so both writers stay in sync with the declared pointer paths.

packages/serato/src/geob.test.ts.content: Only single-marker BeatGrids are ever exercised here (and in the other specs, `payload[5]` is always 1). The per-marker loop in `parseBeatGrid` reads marker `i` at offsets `6 + i*8` / `10 + i*8`; that offset arithmetic is never validated for `i > 0`, so a wrong stride (e.g. `6 + i*4`) or a count read from the wrong byte would go undetected. Add a two-marker fixture (count = 2 with distinct `pos`/`bpm`) and pin both regions.

The comment claims a "u32 count", but the parser reads a single byte at `payload[5]` (`const count = payload[5]`). For count = 1 that byte coincides with the low byte of a BE u32, so this fixture cannot distinguish a correct u32-count parser from a u8 byte-5 parser — a real regression in count decoding would still pass. Additionally the terminal byte here is `0x37` while the ScratchBeat vector below and the golden in `index.test.ts` use `0x00`, and the parser never validates the footer/version suffix, so the disagreement is silent. Reconcile the fixtures and (if the format defines it) assert the expected terminal byte.

packages/serato/src/geob.test.ts.content: All three rejection cases use a bare `toThrow()` with no message/type matcher, so an unrelated failure (or an overly broad guard that rejects everything) still passes. Pin the expected error shape, e.g. `toThrow(/version=2/)` for the wrong-version case and `/truncated/` for the short case, so the test verifies *why* it throws.

`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)` is only a lower bound; the fallback region for 60 BPM is exactly 4 beats (`count = round((60/60*4)/(60/60)) = 4`), so an over-extended expansion (e.g. a rounding bug yielding 8 beats) would still satisfy this assertion, and the test title ("past four beats") misstates the intent. Assert the exact length (and optionally the last beat time) to catch both under- and over-extension.

Two issues with this helper. (1) `for..of` yields code points, but `ch.charCodeAt(0)` returns only the first UTF-16 unit, so a non-BMP path (emoji/CJK extension) is encoded as 2 bytes instead of 4 — the length field and payload become wrong and the fixture would silently diverge from the real format. Iterate code units instead (e.g. `for (const unit of s) out.push(0, unit.charCodeAt(0))`). (2) The crate fixture is assembled with the exact layout the parser assumes, so it is self-referential: a wrong real-world layout (UTF-16LE vs BE, wrong length endianness) would still pass. Add a real/golden `.crate` byte fixture to validate against a known-good source.

packages/serato/src/mapping.test.ts.content: The "without cross-talk" test only asserts `state.deckId`, which is merely the input echoed back by the stateless mapper. It cannot detect cross-talk/state leakage between decks (e.g. if track/loop/fader values from deck 1 were reused for deck 2). Assert at least one non-deckId field per deck (track path, loop, channelFader/crossfader, receivedAtNs) so the test would actually fail on leakage.

Loop-coalescing coverage gap: only the `trackChanged=true && loopActive=false` branch is exercised. But the mapper (index.ts:66-68) only resets the loop in the `!loopActive` branch; with `trackChanged=true && loopActive=true` it keeps the previous `loopStartSeconds/loopEndSeconds/loopBeatLength`. Stale loop bounds from the previous track would therefore silently persist, and the current tests still pass. Add a case with `trackChanged=true, loopActive=true` plus stale loop values to pin the intended behavior.

This "re-asserted loop on the same track" case reuses `base` with `trackChanged=false`, so it never re-asserts a loop after an actual track change, and its assertions (`loop.active`, `loop.beatLength`, track path) duplicate the first test. Suggest driving it through a track change (`trackChanged=true, loopActive=true` with fresh loop start/end/beatLength) or removing it, so it adds independent verification.
